title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 330 (Certain transfers to be void)

content.overview: Any transfer or assignment by a company of all its properties or assets to trustees for the benefit of all its creditors is void.
content.glance: A general assignment of all assets to trustees for all creditors is void.
content.study: Section 330 strikes down a blanket transfer or assignment of the whole of a company’s properties or assets to trustees for the benefit of all its creditors. Such a disposition is void. The provision prevents informal collective arrangements that would otherwise bypass the statutory winding-up machinery and the orderly ranking of claims.

sections.heading: Void general assignment
sections.body: Transfer or assignment of all properties or assets to trustees for the benefit of all creditors is void.

examples.title: Assignment to trustees
examples.body: A distressed company executes a deed assigning all its assets to trustees to hold for the benefit of all creditors. The assignment is void under s. 330; creditors must proceed under the statutory winding-up or IBC regime.

hypotheticals.question: Is a partial security assignment to a single creditor void under s. 330?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 330 targets a transfer or assignment of all properties or assets to trustees for the benefit of all creditors; a limited security to one creditor is outside its scope (though other avoidance provisions may apply).

rows.left: All assets to trustees for all creditors
rows.right: Any non-ordinary-course / non-good-faith transfer within one year

misconceptions.trap: Any assignment for the benefit of creditors is automatically valid if all creditors consent.
misconceptions.correction: A transfer of all properties or assets to trustees for the benefit of all creditors is void under s. 330 regardless of consent.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 330 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify whether there is a transfer/assignment of all properties or assets. II. Check whether it is to trustees for the benefit of all creditors. III. Conclude voidness if both conditions are met.

examTips: Emphasise the ‘all properties or assets’ and ‘trustees for the benefit of all creditors’ elements.
revisionPoints: General assignment of all assets to trustees for all creditors is void
